title: Prose lint sweep across docs, skills and osf test comments
summary: A repository-wide prose and reference cleanup. The `osf` prose linter's rules were tightened, and this change brings the repository's own Markdown and Rust doc comments into line with them: vague time words ('today', 'currently') are replaced with concrete ones, bare 'decision NNNN' references become relative Markdown links, quoted UI strings lose their scare quotes, and a few long sentences are split. Two Rust test files change only in doc comments; no executable code changes. The one substantive content edit is in the skill-lint research note, where SkillEvaluator's three tiers become a table and a few numeric claims are reworded.

lanes.subtitle: Markdown, skills and Rust doc comments
lanes.summary: The prose that the linter reads: repository docs, skill files and the doc comments on Rust tests.

lanes.label: osf CLI
lanes.subtitle: crates/osf
lanes.summary: The command-line tool that lints prose and skill files, scans for forbidden text, reports change risk and maintains the pull-request status block.

lanes.subtitle: Rules and findings

nodes.label: Documentation corpus
nodes.subtitle: docs/**, README, CONTRIBUTING
nodes.summary: The architecture, design, product, research and vision documents. This change rewrites vague time words, converts bare decision references into relative links, removes scare quotes and splits long sentences.

nodes.label: Skill files
nodes.subtitle: skills/**/SKILL.md
nodes.summary: The pr-outline skill's step 6 now names the file tree and the diff block instead of referring back to step numbers, so the instruction survives reordering.

nodes.label: hook.rs test comments
nodes.subtitle: crates/osf/src/hook.rs
nodes.summary: Two doc comments lose their 'Change 3:' prefix. The test bodies, names and assertions are untouched.

nodes.label: skill_lint.rs test comments
nodes.subtitle: crates/osf/tests/skill_lint.rs
nodes.summary: Two doc comments lose their 'Change 1:' and 'Change 2:' prefixes and are rewrapped. The fixtures and assertions are untouched.

nodes.label: osf
nodes.subtitle: cargo run -p osf
nodes.summary: The only runnable artifact today. It lints prose and skill files, scans for text that must never reach a public repository, reports change risk and keeps a status block on a pull request.

nodes.label: Prose lint
nodes.subtitle: writing rules over the body
nodes.summary: Reads a document's body and reports findings such as long sentences and vague time words. The rules are what this change is conforming to, not what it changes.

nodes.label: Skill lint
nodes.subtitle: frontmatter and body
nodes.summary: Validates a SKILL.md: structure, headings, frontmatter and the writing rules over the body. A finding's line must point at the real line in the file, past a folded description.

nodes.label: Line mapping
nodes.subtitle: body offset to file line
nodes.summary: Translates a position inside the extracted body back to the line number a reader would see in SKILL.md. The test that guards it is one of the two whose comment changed.

nodes.label: Lint workflow
nodes.subtitle: GitHub Actions
nodes.summary: Runs the lint over the repository on every pull request. This change is the corpus catching up with what that job already enforces.

edges.label: documents
edges.summary: The documentation corpus is the input the prose rules read. Every rewrite in this change is a document being made to satisfy a rule that already existed.

edges.label: SKILL.md
edges.summary: Skill files are linted as structured text with headings, frontmatter and a body. The pr-outline edit is a skill file being made to read unambiguously.
The skill lint asks the line mapping where a body finding really sits in the file.
The hook tests exercise the stop-hook and prompt behaviour of the osf binary. Only their doc comments changed.
The integration tests drive the skill lint over fixtures. Only their doc comments changed.

edges.label: cargo run -p osf
edges.summary: Continuous integration runs the osf binary under the workflow's own token, which no agent holds. That run is the authority.

flows.title: A document passes through the prose lint
flows.summary: What happens when the linter reads one of the documents this change rewrote. The rules are unchanged; the document is what moved.

messages.label: read body
messages.note: The linter extracts the body, skipping frontmatter and fenced code.

messages.label: apply writing rules
messages.note: Long sentences, vague time words and similar rules run over the extracted body.

messages.label: body offset
messages.note: A finding inside the body is mapped back to the line a reader would see in the file.

messages.label: findings, exit status
messages.note: In continuous integration the exit status is what gates the pull request.

views.title: Where the lint sits
views.summary: The authoring surface on the left, the osf tool and its rules in the middle, continuous integration on the right. This change touches only the leftmost lane.

views.title: Inside the lint engine
views.summary: The two rule sets and the line mapping they share. None of these changed; they are the contract the rewritten prose is being made to satisfy.

views.title: A document through the prose lint
views.summary: Read, apply rules, map the finding back to a real file line, report. The document is the only thing that moved.
